result.summary: Narrow B2B accessibility remediation for SMEs with public websites, sold as a fixed-scope fix instead of a vague SEO or compliance promise.
result.opportunity: Many small business websites still have obvious accessibility issues (insufficient contrast, unlabeled form fields, missing alt text, weak keyboard focus) that hurt usability and can be fixed quickly with a bounded package. This is a real pain because web owners often cannot see the problem and it is easier to sell as a clear practical improvement than as a broad legal-compliance service.
result.target_customer: Spanish SMEs with public websites and contact funnels: clinics, local service firms, real-estate agencies, small consultancies, and local businesses with 5-50 employees and a public website that generates leads.
result.offer: A 3-day accessibility quick-fix pack: public-site audit of 3-5 pages, prioritized remediation of obvious issues (contrast, labels, focus, keyboard navigation, image alt text), patch applied or provided in a staging copy, and a before/after QA summary. No legal-compliance guarantee; only a practical remediation scope.
result.price: 149 EUR for the 3-page audit + quick-fix pack; 299 EUR for up to 10 pages or a second pass
result.why_now: Accessibility issues are common in real websites, W3C publishes concrete WCAG guidance, and the WebAIM Million project shows a large share of public pages still fail basic checks. Small businesses often know they need a better digital experience but do not know which fixes matter most, which makes a specific, low-friction remediation package sellable now.
actions_completed: Reviewed repository context, playbook seeds, and recent competitor attempts to avoid repeating crowded offers.
Confirmed CobrAMO is payment infrastructure and not a lead list or customer source.
Reviewed public accessibility guidance and issue prevalence data from W3C and WebAIM.
Selected a narrower, lower-friction offer than the saturated local-review and Shopify-feed patterns.

execution_packet.channel: Personalized email to founders or marketing managers of small Spanish businesses via public contact pages and company websites
execution_packet.subject: Quick accessibility fix for your public website
execution_packet.message: Hi [Name], I reviewed your public site and noticed a few obvious accessibility issues that can be fixed without changing your whole website: low-contrast links or buttons, form fields without labels, weak keyboard focus, and missing alt text on key images. I do a small, fixed-scope accessibility remediation pack for 3-5 pages: contrast and readability fixes, form and label cleanup, keyboard focus improvements, image text alternatives, and a short QA summary with before/after notes. This is a practical improvement package, not a legal-compliance guarantee. Fixed price: 149 EUR. If this is useful, I can send a 2-minute sample audit for one page and show exactly what I would change. Reference: RANK-IAMO513.
execution_packet.deliverable: A short accessibility report, prioritized fix list, updated HTML/CSS patches or staging-copy adjustments, before/after screenshots, and a final QA checklist.

result.differentiation_from_previous: I did not repeat the crowded GBP/review and Shopify feed patterns. This offer is narrower, easier to explain, and less dependent on broad SEO claims: it sells a clear, visible remediation pack for real accessibility defects, with explicit limits and no legal-compliance overstatement.
result.next_step: Identify 15-20 Spanish SMEs with public sites and obvious a11y issues; inspect 2-3 concrete defects on each site; send one personalized note with two exact issues and the fixed price; if there is interest, send a sample audit and close the first 149 EUR pilot through CobrAMO with reference RANK-IAMO513.
result.notes: The strongest playbook fit is route #33 Accessibility audit and remediation pack, with route #31 (website technical audit) and #34 (web performance optimization) as adjacent but not primary. The key is to keep scope fixed and practical rather than claiming legal compliance or broad accessibility certification. This is more saleable than broad SEO packages because the problem is visible in the public site itself and the fix has a clear before/after outcome.
